title: Circuitous fallback gestures — lab journal
body:
Context:
Small, messy scratchpad tracking an odd failover pattern observed during the 2026-03-04 surge window. Not a formal postmortem yet — just breadcrumbs and commands so I don't lose the repro. Patchy timestamps are from tracing + logs.

Summary of observed behavior (short):
- Certain customer routes (mainly long-context chat sessions) were ejected from primary region (us-west-2) and bounced to eu-west-1 as a fallback despite healthy host-level metrics in us-west-2.
- Ejects were not correlated with obvious GPU OOMs or node reboots. Instead we saw a sustained stream of route-eject events tied to late KV cache hits and subsequent policy-eject decisions.
- Repro is intermittent; appears when batched request queue depth spikes and prefix-KV cache thrash happens.

Key trace excerpts (anonymized):
- 2026-03-04T22:18:07Z request_id=r-0a9c path=/v1/generate model=redwood-four-32k primary=us-west-2 trace=trace-9f7
  runtime: batch_enqueue=12ms queue_wait=210ms kernel_dispatch=36ms kv_lookup=142ms kv_miss_count=1 policy_eval=8ms policy_action=eject(fallback=eu-west-1, reason=kv_latency)
- 2026-03-04T22:18:08Z request_id= r-0aa0 path=/v1/generate same-session
  policy: prefer-region=us-west-2 score=0.92 fallback_score_eu=0.88 eval_threshold=0.9 decision=eject -> routed to eu-west-1

Interesting error snippets from control-plane logs:
- WARN smart-router: policy-election drift detected: moving-avg(kv_lookup_ms)=87 -> sudden-spike(142) for route=acct-22/session-991
- ERROR route-manager: attempted-route-override failed: ERR_ROUTE_MUTATION (expected pinned-version v7, got v6)
- INFO telemetry: prefix-cache-evictions=217 per-min, tail_latency_p90=480ms

Commands I ran (local replicate attempts):
- curl to router decision endpoint: 
  curl -s -X POST https://router-staging.redwood/api/v1/eval -H 'Authorization: Bearer dev' -d '{"route":"acct-22","session_meta":{"seq_len":12000,"last_token_ts":167}}' | jq
  -> got decision: {"action":"eject","target":"eu-west-1","reason":"kv_latency"}

- kubectl logs -n serving runner-usw2-3 -c runtime | grep 'policy_action' -n | tail -n50\\  (look for correlation with prefix-cache events)

- curl health endpoints for runtime on a sample pod: 
  curl -s http://10.10.5.92:9090/health | jq
  -> {"ok":true,"memory_gb":41,"gpu_util":22,"queued":6}  (pod-level health didn't explain eject)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Conservative policy election math + noisy KV latency signal: our policy uses moving averages with smoothing constant tuned for slower changes. When queue depth jumps, the quick transient spike in KV lookup time can push policy into eject territory before the host-level health signals stabilize. In short: signal mismatch and asymmetric reaction.
2) CGR (circuit gating rules) interaction: when prefix-cache eviction rate exceeds threshold, an internal flag flips which lowers prefer-region score by a hard delta. That delta might be too large, causing unnecessary cross-region failovers for borderline cases.
3) Stale model pin mismatch path: route-manager saw a version mismatch entry around same time (ERR_ROUTE_MUTATION). If route-manager temporarily rejects in-region traffic for version safety while fallback allowed, that could trigger redirect. Need to check whether route-manager rejects are being interpreted as policy-ejects downstream.
4) Telemetry sampling aliasing: our p90 tail latency is reported per-minute; if bucket boundaries line up with surge, the snapshot used by policy-eval might be stale/unrepresentative.

Quick reproducer steps to try in lab:
- Start a synthetic load generator targeting a route with large seq_len (>=12k) and mix of cold vs warm KV prefixes. Ramp queue depth to 100+ across the dataset.
- Instrument moving-average window sizes in the staging router config: set smoothing alpha from 0.1 -> 0.03 to see if policy becomes less jumpy.
- Toggle CGR prefix-eviction hard-delta to a smaller value and run the same load.
- Force a route-manager version mismatch in staging to observe downstream routing reaction (deliberate PATCH that returns 409 on route pin check).

Notes on config bits I inspected: (snippets pulled from staging config)
- smart-routing.policy_evaluation.window_ms = 60000
- smart-routing.kv_signal.alpha = 0.12
- route-manager.accept_version_conflict = false
- cgr.prefix_eviction.hard_delta = 0.35  # effectively reduces prefer_score by 35% when tripped

Preliminary quick wins (low risk):
- Reduce hard_delta to 0.15 in staging for susceptible routes (A/B test).
- Add short cooldown on policy-eject when queue_wait > 300ms but host health ok (prevent immediate cross-region ejection for transient backpressure).
- Add extra telemetry tag to route-eject events: include route-pinned-version so we can correlate ERR_ROUTE_MUTATION events.

Longer-term changes to consider: 
- Introduce differential smoothing: give host-level health (OOMs, GPU util) a faster alpha than KV signals so transient KV blips don't dominate.
- Revisit CGR thresholds; convert hard cutoff to sigmoid dampening so that evictions have graded impact.
- Add canary where policy-eval will simulate-evaluate fallback but not actually eject for 30s, just tag events. If safe, escalate to full eject.

Questions to ask/offload:
- @Jonah: can you pull full trace for request_id r-0a9c and export the full batch payload? I want to see whether the KV miss was on a hot prefix or a completely new prefix.
- @Ellen: can you grep control-plane logs for ERR_ROUTE_MUTATION around 22:17-22:20 and dump correlated route-manager pod logs? Link them here when you have.

Quick dump of interesting metrics around window (2026-03-04T22:15 - 22:25):
- prefix-cache-evictions/min: 180 -> spike to 220 at 22:18
- queue_length_avg per pod (usw2): 8 -> 72 at surge
- cross-region-ejects count (system-wide): 3 in 10m (but concentrated on two customer routes)

Immediate next steps I'm going to try today (check off):
- [x] Re-run decision API call with synthetic payloads, vary seq_len and prefix entropy.
- [ ] Spin up staging load generator with warm/cold prefix mix and reproduce.
- [ ] Apply lower hard_delta in staging and run A/B.
- [ ] Short cooldown on eject rule (prototype in router staging).
- [ ] Add route-pinned-version to eject telemetry (PR draft: gh PR/2784 is initial patch).

Triage notes/end-of-day:
- This smells like a signal-fusion/bandwidth problem more than a pure infra outage. Host-level health is not failing — the control plane is deciding to eject based on noisy signal. Fix path likely in policy tuning and adding guardrails (cooldowns, graded penalties).
- Will collect more traces and paste here. If we can reproduce reliably in staging then we push change. If not reproducible, instrument more aggressively and rollout telemetry-only canary first.

-- Samira
(keeping this in users/ so I can fetch from mobile while on call)
